11月WTI原油期货合约整周都在权衡霍尔木兹海峡可能重新开放的前景与航运状况尚未恢复正常的风险。周二，在有报道称伊朗可能在7天内重新开放该海峡后，该合约跌至88.67美元；随后于周四反弹至96.78美元，因为外交层面的消息遇到了整周一直存在的相同问题：没有达成协议、没有正常的油轮通航，也没有证据表明现货市场已恢复常态。

截至格林威治标准时间周四22:00，11月WTI原油期货报每桶94.76美元，本周下跌0.71美元或0.74%。市场虽已脱离本周高点，但也远高于周二的低点。这道出了实情：当沙特原油开始流动且伊朗抛出协议可能时，交易员剔除了部分风险溢价；而当事实证明替代航线并不等同于开放的航道时，他们又重新计入了部分溢价。

沙特和伊拉克原油改变了原油交易格局

本周伊始，流入市场的原油数量增多，而此前该市场已被计入了更严重的供应问题溢价。在袭击损坏沙特阿美东西管道并扰乱部分红海装载后，沙特阿美增加了通过霍尔木兹海峡的发运量。油轮追踪数据显示，在波斯湾内有约1400万桶原油装上了7艘超大型油轮（VLCC）。沙特经由该海峡的原油流量较8月水平大幅上升。

东西管道的重启提供了另一种选择。虽然这并未完全恢复至正常运力，但它为沙特阿拉伯提供了一条通往红海的路线，无需每桶原油都通过霍尔木兹海峡。伊拉克也表示可以增加经由土耳其的出口量。

这些都是实实在在的原油和实实在在的路线。这就是为什么在市场达成外交协议之前原油就遭到抛售。如果有更多原油能够运抵买家手中，交易员无需等待和平协议就会削减部分溢价。

目前的运输成本依然高昂且脆弱。生产商正通过阿曼近海的船对船过驳、军事护航以及调整装载计划来维持出口运作。原油确实在流动，但流经的系统成本更高、耗时更长，并且可能会因一次袭击而再次中断。路透社报道称，尽管生产商通过替代方案维持出口，但霍尔木兹海峡可见的船只通航量仍远低于战前水平。

伊朗提供了一条路径，而非直接放行

在共同社报道称如果美国缓解军事压力、伊朗可能在7天内重新开放霍尔木兹海峡后，周二的抛售加剧。市场对这一头条新闻做出了剧烈反应，仿佛海峡已经在重新开放。

事情从来没有那么简单。伊朗的立场是有条件的。美国并未宣布达成协议。保险、安全通行、油轮通航以及成品油流动并没有突然恢复正常。

原因显而易见。双方今年早些时候曾有过类似的框架协议，但最终破裂。关于谈判的报道会改变市场预期，但只要油轮仍未在无军事护航的情况下通行、保险市场尚未开始降低风险定价，航线实际状况就不会改变。

柴油未跟随原油走低

原油市场本周迎来了供应缓解，但柴油市场并未如此。

欧洲瓦斯油较布伦特原油的溢价创下接近每桶95美元的历史新高。美国柴油价格仍高于每加仑6美元。成品油的短缺源于炼油厂运转和成品油流动受阻，而不仅仅是原油供应不足。

这一区别至关重要。沙特阿拉伯可以改变原油货运路线，伊拉克可以通过土耳其输送更多石油。但当中东成品油流动受阻、炼油厂已满负荷运转时，这些举措都无法为欧洲额外增加一桶柴油。

在《政客》（Politico）报道称美国政府正考虑实行为期90天的柴油出口禁令后，白宫又增添了一层不确定性。白宫随后否认了该报道。虽然该政策尚未出台，但这一构想表明压力正在何处积聚。限制出口或许能增加美国境内的供应，但这也会抽走欧洲的供应，而欧洲已经在为馏分油支付创纪录的溢价。

成品油市场仍在提醒原油交易员，不要对供应缓解感到过于乐观。原油可能会因有关沙特出口的报道而下跌，但柴油需要炼油厂产出和正常贸易流恢复后，其溢价才会消退。

库存数据展现同样的分化

美国能源信息署（EIA）报告称，在截至9月18日当周，美国商业原油库存增加了300万桶，至4.264亿桶。分析师此前预期为下降。这在沙特和伊拉克供应途径改善后，给卖家提供了进一步打压原油的理由。

馏分油库存则呈现出截然不同的局面。其库存减少了42.8万桶，至1.074亿桶。降幅虽然不大，但发生时柴油和瓦斯油的溢价已处于极高水平。

商业原油库存正在增加，成品油供应依然偏紧。战略石油储备（SPR）已降至接近2.85亿桶，为商业体系提供的缓冲减少。这就是原油和柴油市场在同一周内释放不同信号的原因。

11月WTI原油期货周线技术分析

趋势指标分析

11月WTI原油期货本周小幅走高，但市场已接近形成周线收盘价反转顶部。该合约触及101.69美元的新主高点后掉头下行。上周收盘价为95.86美元。若周线收于该水平下方，将确认反转形态。这虽不会改变依然向上的主要趋势，但可能导致动能转向下行。

最近的次要底部为78.55美元，主要底部为67.09美元。短期回撤目标是位于90.12美元的50%回撤位，下一个下行目标是位于84.39美元的主要50%回撤位。这两个位置都远高于位于70.62美元的上升52周移动平均线。在上行方面，若突破101.69美元，则将恢复上升趋势，并打开通往先前高点104.44美元和110.08美元的大门。

周度技术预测

截至10月2日当周的11月原油期货周线合约走势，可能将取决于交易员对95.18美元关口的反应。

若能持续守在95.18美元上方，将发出买盘存在的信号。如果消息面再次转向利多，这将使市场有可能重新测试101.69美元的合约高点。潜在的上行目标包括104.44美元和110.08美元。

若持续跌破95.18美元，则将表明买盘正在放缓、抛压正在增加。如果引发足够的下行动能，我们可能会看到行情重新测试88.67美元。若跌破该水平，将发出涨势正在减弱的强烈信号，其他潜在目标为84.39美元和78.67美元。

市场降低了波斯湾立即发生供应冲击的概率，但尚未完全按正常石油贸易计价。沙特的石油正在运输。伊拉克正在增加供应选项。船对船转运正使部分海湾原油保持流动。只要这些进展持续，就会限制油价的上行空间。

风险在于，交易员们已经在未达成协议的情况下两次消化了外交斡旋的预期。如果谈判促成油轮正常通航、降低保险成本并恢复霍尔木兹海峡的常规航运，原油的风险溢价可能会进一步被挤出。如果谈判破裂、沙特基础设施再次遇袭，或柴油库存持续下降，现货市场将重新掌握主导权。

本周从97.22美元跌至88.67美元、随后又反弹至96.78美元的走势，展现出市场在两个方向上重新定价的速度有多快。原油市场的供应压力有所缓解。柴油市场则依然短缺。

从技术面来看，在截至9月18日的一周内，价格在101.69美元处形成了一个收盘价反转顶部。这意味着我们所面对的不是一个普通的高点。它除了是一项看跌指标外，也是加速上行的触发点。因此，如果重新涌入的买盘将其突破，请牢记这一点。

下行目标位为50%回撤位，包括90.12美元、84.39美元和78.67美元。买方会将它们视为价值区间。鉴于主要趋势依然向上，市场很可能仍处于“逢低买入”模式。

只有当卖方开始跌破78.55美元、72.05美元和67.09美元的波段低点时，交易员们才需要担心趋势反转的问题。

最重要的是，位于71.21美元的52周均线仍保持着主要的长期上涨趋势完好无损。

topStories.fullContent: Saudi Aramco has restarted its East-West pipeline Petroline less than two weeks after attacks knocked out the 7 million bpd system, restoring at least some of the route that has carried the bulk of Saudi crude around the Strait of Hormuz since the war began. Pumping has resumed at reduced rates, with Aramco reportedly targeting around 4 million bpd as flows gradually rebuild. Tanker loadings at Yanbu also appear to have restarted this week, although regular exports have yet to recover. Industrial Info Resources cited satellite imagery showing vessels taking on crude, while Reuters reported that Aramco had told European refiners it first needed to build a "critical mass" of crude at Yanbu. Two tankers scheduled to load September 23 had not done so, with another six scheduled between September 24 and 27. According to Kpler, the pipeline had been moving roughly 5.5 million bpd before the September attack, including about 4.5 million bpd destined for export from Yanbu. Kpler says the pipeline itself suffered limited damage, with the heavier damage concentrated at the pumping infrastructure. At least one pumping station was extensively damaged, and Aramco has been installing a temporary bypass while permanent repairs continue. Kpler had initially estimated four to six weeks for permanent repairs because of damage to pumping equipment and the time required to obtain replacement components. Yanbu was exporting roughly 4 million to 4.5 million bpd before the attack, compared with about 750,000 bpd before the war, according to MEES. The disruption also forced the 400,000 bpd SAMREF refinery at Yanbu to cut operations by around half, with Industrial Info expecting reduced rates to continue into October. Petroline had rarely operated anywhere near its 7 million bpd capacity before the war, but Aramco pushed substantially more crude west as traffic through Hormuz fell. MEES estimates the pipeline allowed Saudi Arabia to maintain roughly 65% of its prewar oil exports outside the strait, turning Yanbu from a secondary outlet into one of the kingdom's principal export routes. Much of that crude continued east to Saudi Arabia's traditional Asian customers. S&P Global puts second-quarter Yanbu loadings at 3.9 million bpd, more than double year-earlier levels, with roughly 80% headed east of Suez. South Korean and Japanese refiners were already planning to continue lifting Saudi crude through Yanbu even if Hormuz returned to normal. The attack temporarily forced Aramco back through the route Petroline was supposed to avoid. Lloyd's List Intelligence says Saudi-linked VLCC transits through Hormuz reached their highest weekly level since the war began after the pipeline went down, with Riyadh shifting more exports east while Yanbu was effectively cut off. Lloyd's expects Saudi-controlled tanker traffic through the strait to remain elevated as Aramco works through spot sales and Yanbu gradually returns. So, the million-dollar question now is whether the Houthis will have the will or wherewithal to continue targeting Saudi oil facilities. They answered at least part of that question Thursday, launching another barrage against Saudi Arabia just as Aramco was trying to restore Petroline and Yanbu exports. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Yanbu and Taif, while the Houthis later said they had launched missiles and drones against Aramco facilities in Yanbu and a "sensitive target" in Riyadh. There were no immediate reports that Aramco facilities were hit. The latest attack follows Houthi claims that they targeted Aramco facilities in Yanbu on September 16 and September 19, giving Aramco three attempted attacks around its principal Red Sea oil hub in little more than a week. The drones that struck the East-West Pipeline were launched from Iraq's Maysan governorate near the Iranian border, according to Saudi and Iraqi authorities; the Islamic Resistance in Iraq denies responsibility. The cost of using Yanbu is rising even when the missiles miss. War-risk insurance for Saudi-linked tankers loading there has tripled in recent weeks to around 3% of a vessel's value, from less than 1% in early July, according to Reuters, putting the premium for a $100 million tanker at roughly $3 million for a single voyage. Rates can reach 7% at Saudi ports farther south, where vessels are more exposed to Houthi attacks around Bab al Mandab. Hormuz remains more expensive at roughly 6% to 9%, but the difference between Saudi Arabia's two export routes has narrowed considerably as the security situation in the Red Sea has deteriorated. Riyadh had spent months reorganizing Yemen's disparate anti-Houthi forces under Saudi sponsorship, only to watch them collapse during their first major test when the Houthis swept down the Red Sea coast earlier this month. Saudi aircraft have stepped up strikes across Yemen while government forces have stopped the Houthi advance into the mountains above Bab al Mandab and begun taking back some of the high ground, including Jabal Qarfan and Jabal Zalat this week. The Houthis still hold their coastal gains, including Mokha and positions around Bab al Mandab, but they have so far failed to take the mountain barrier needed to secure them. Maritime traffic through Bab al Mandab has meanwhile fallen to around 30 vessels a day from roughly 80 normally, according to Dryad Global. But the Houthis, of course, are not the only threat. Riyadh held off retaliating for the attack on Petroline after Baghdad asked for time to deal with the militias operating from Iraqi territory, but their strike capability hasn't been dismantled, and a month's-end deadline for the state to seize militia weapons is going to be watered down significantly to the point that the weapons will most likely just move along with the militias into the state security structures except for those who resist outright. It's hardly the answer Riyadh was looking for. The pipeline is relaunching, but the threats have not been neutralized.
topStories.fullTranslation:
在袭击导致日输送能力达700万桶的东西输油管道（Petroline）瘫痪不到两周后，沙特阿美（Saudi Aramco）已重启该管线。自战争爆发以来，沙特大部分原油正是通过该路线绕过霍尔木兹海峡进行运输，此番重启至少恢复了部分运力。输油已在降速状态下恢复，据报道，随着输送量逐步回升，沙特阿美的目标是达到约400万桶/日。延布港的油轮装载作业本周似乎也已重启，尽管常规出口尚未恢复。工业信息资源公司（Industrial Info Resources）援引卫星图像称已有油轮在装载原油，而路透社报道称，沙特阿美已告知欧洲炼油商，首先需要在延布建立原油的“临界规模”。原定于9月23日装载的两艘油轮尚未作业，另有六艘定于9月24日至27日之间装载。

根据Kpler的数据，在9月份遭遇袭击前，该管道的日运量约为550万桶，其中包括约450万桶运往延布供出口的原油。Kpler指出，管道本身受损有限，更严重的损坏集中在泵送基础设施上。至少有一座泵站受到严重破坏，在进行永久性修复的同时，沙特阿美一直在安装临时旁路。Kpler最初估计永久性修复需要4到6周时间，因为泵送设备受损且获取替换部件需要时间。据《中东经济调查》（MEES）报道，袭击发生前，延布港的原油出口量约为400万至450万桶/日，而战前仅约为75万桶/日。此次供应中断还迫使延布日产能40万桶的SAMREF炼油厂将作业量削减了约一半，工业信息资源公司预计降负荷运行将持续至10月份。

在战前，东西管道的实际运行负荷极少接近其700万桶/日的额定运能，但随着霍尔木兹海峡通行量下降，沙特阿美向西输送的原油量大幅增加。MEES估计，该管道使沙特阿拉伯得以在霍尔木兹海峡之外维持战前约65%的石油出口量，从而将延布从次要出口枢纽转变为该国的主要出口通道之一。其中大部分原油随后继续向东运往沙特传统的亚洲客户手中。标普全球（S&P Global）的数据显示，延布第二季度的装船量达390万桶/日，比去年同期翻了一倍以上，其中约80%运往苏伊士以东。韩国和日本的炼油商此前就已计划，即使霍尔木兹海峡恢复正常，也将继续在延布提取沙特原油。

此次袭击暂时迫使沙特阿美重新启用东西管道本打算规避的航道。劳氏海事情报（Lloyd's List Intelligence）表示，在管道停运后，与沙特相关的超大型油轮（VLCC）过境霍尔木兹海峡的周度频次达到了战以来的最高水平，因为在延布港运力实质上被切断期间，利雅得将更多出口转向了东线。劳氏预计，随着沙特阿美加紧处理现货销售以及延布港逐步恢复，沙特控制的通过海峡的油轮运输量将保持高位。

因此，现在至关重要的问题是胡塞武装是否有意愿或能力继续打击沙特石油设施。他们在周四至少部分回答了这个问题：就在沙特阿美试图恢复东西管道和延布出口之际，胡塞武装对沙特阿拉伯发动了新一轮集中打击。沙特阿拉伯表示，拦截了瞄准延布和塔伊夫的6枚胡塞弹道导弹；而胡塞武装随后表示，已向延布的阿美设施以及利雅得的一处“敏感目标”发射了导弹和无人机。目前尚无阿美设施遇袭受损的直接报告。在此次最新袭击之前，胡塞武装曾声称于9月16日和9月19日袭击了延布的阿美设施，这意味着阿美的主要红海石油枢纽在短短一周多的时间里遭受了三次袭击企图。据沙特和伊拉克当局称，袭击东西输油管道的无人机是从靠近伊朗边境的伊拉克米桑省发射的；伊拉克伊斯兰抵抗组织对此否认承担责任。

即使导弹偏离目标，使用延布的成本也正在攀升。据路透社报道，最近几周，在延布装载原油的沙特关联油轮的战争风险险率已从7月初的不足1%增加至船体价值的3%左右，这意味着一艘价值1亿美元的油轮单次航程保费约为300万美元。在更偏南方的沙特港口，费率可高达7%，那里的船只更容易受到曼德海峡周边胡塞武装的袭击。霍尔木兹海峡的险率仍然更高，大约在6%到9%之间，但随着红海安全局势恶化，沙特阿拉伯这两大出口通道之间的成本差距已显著缩小。

利雅得此前数月一直致力于在沙特主持下重组也门分散的反胡塞武装力量，然而在本月早些时候胡塞武装席卷红海沿岸时，这些力量在初次大考中便溃退瓦解。沙特战机已加大对也门全境的打击力度，与此同时，政府军阻挡了胡塞武装向曼德海峡上方山区的推进，并于本周开始夺回部分高地，包括卡尔凡山（Jabal Qarfan）和扎拉特山（Jabal Zalat）。胡塞武装目前仍守住了其沿海战果，包括摩卡港（Mokha）以及曼德海峡周边据点，但迄今为止尚未攻克用于巩固这些据点所需的山地屏障。根据德里亚德海事（Dryad Global）的数据，穿行曼德海峡的海上交通量已从平时的每日约80艘锐减至目前的约30艘。

当然，胡塞武装并非唯一的威胁。在巴格达方面请求给予时间处理活跃于伊拉克境内的民兵组织后，利雅得暂缓了针对东西管道遇袭的报复行动，但这些民兵的打击能力并未被彻底瓦解；此外，原本定于月底前由政府收缴民兵武器的期限将被大幅淡化妥协，其结果极可能是武器随同民兵直接被收编入国家安全机构，仅有公开抗拒者除外。这绝非利雅得所期待的答案。输油管道正在重新启动，但各方威胁并未被消除。

topStories.fullContent: Another Russian refinery was taken offline on Friday following a Ukrainian drone attack, in a sign that Ukraine and Russia continue to trade strikes on energy infrastructure despite separate talks with U.S. officials in New York aimed at de-escalation. The Novoshakhtinsk refinery in the southern Russian region of Rostov was hit by drones and had to be taken offline, regional governor Yury Slyusar said in a post on Telegram early on Friday. As a result of the drone attacks, the Novoshakhtinsk refinery, which has the capacity to process 110,000 barrels of crude oil per day, was damaged and halted operations, the official said. Ukraine continues its campaign to cripple Russian refining capacity, fuel supply, and export revenues. Due to the low refinery production, Russia has been forced to ban diesel exports for months and is likely to extend the ban beyond September 30. The ban was initially introduced in July as Ukraine has continuously taken Russian refineries offline. Last week, Ukraine hit an oil refinery near Moscow, damaging a processing plant co-owned by Rosneft and Gazprom Neft. Recent attacks from both sides show that there isn't any truce in attacking energy sites. Ukraine's forces hit the refinery in Yaroslavl with drones last week, while Russia attacked infrastructure in Kyiv. Russian daily Vedomosti reported last week that the government would extend its ban on diesel exports for all fuel producers to October 31, due to delayed refinery maintenance and the need to rebuild fuel reserves before winter. Russia has been suffering from a gasoline and diesel crunch since the spring, when Ukraine intensified its drone attacks at Russian refineries, aiming to cripple fuel supply to the front lines and to the domestic Russian market. The Russian ban on diesel exports has added to the Middle East crisis to tighten global middle distillate markets.  By Tsvetana Paraskova for Oilprice.com

周五，又一家俄罗斯炼油厂在遭遇乌克兰无人机袭击后被迫停运。这表明，尽管双方在纽约分别与美国官员举行了旨在缓和局势的会谈，但乌克兰与俄罗斯仍在继续对彼此的能源基础设施发动互袭。

俄罗斯南部罗斯托夫州州长尤里·斯柳萨尔（Yury Slyusar）周五早些时候在Telegram发文称，位于该州的新沙赫金斯克（Novoshakhtinsk）炼油厂遭到无人机袭击，不得不停止运营。该官员表示，无人机袭击导致新沙赫金斯克炼油厂受损并暂停运转，该厂原油日加工能力达11万桶。

乌克兰正在继续推进其削弱俄罗斯炼油能力、燃料供应和出口收入的行动。由于炼油厂产能低下，俄罗斯数月来被迫实施柴油出口禁令，并可能将该禁令延长至9月30日之后。随着乌克兰持续致使俄罗斯炼油厂停运，该禁令最初于7月出台。

上周，乌克兰袭击了莫斯科附近的一处炼油厂，损坏了由俄罗斯石油公司（Rosneft）和俄罗斯天然气工业石油公司（Gazprom Neft）共同拥有的一座加工装置。双方近期的袭击行动表明，对能源设施的打击并无任何停火迹象。乌克兰军队上周使用无人机袭击了雅罗斯拉夫尔的炼油厂，而俄罗斯则袭击了基辅的基础设施。

俄罗斯《新闻报》（Vedomosti）上周报道称，由于炼油厂检修延期以及入冬前重建燃料储备的需要，政府将把针对所有燃料生产商的柴油出口禁令延长至10月31日。自今年春季乌克兰加剧对俄炼油厂的无人机袭击以来，俄罗斯一直饱受汽油和柴油紧缺的困扰，乌方行动旨在切断前线及俄罗斯国内市场的燃料供应。

俄罗斯的柴油出口禁令与中东危机相互叠加，进一步加剧了全球中间馏分油市场的供应紧张。

topStories.title: 考验
topStories.fullContent:
Jensen Huang, the NVIDIA CEO and wearer of the most midlife crisis looking leather jackets in the world, was on Ezra Klein’s podcast. Now I don’t really want you do go through all of what was being said in that recording/writeup. It’s painful. You feel your mental capabilities decaying with every minute of listening … kinda like using a Chatbot. But worse.

Huang says many outrageous things in the podcast. Like when Klein asks about how kids don’t learn skills when using LLMs, Huang responds:

I completely agree. Try to get a kid to do long division right now. The multiplication table is starting to be forgotten. Doing square roots, my goodness. Basic math is being forgotten. Does it matter?[…]Yeah. I don’t think it does. I don’t think it does.

Outrageous. But he needs to go on and top this statement with an even worse one:

There are a lot of skills that don’t matter. My first confession, I actually don’t know my address. […] It’s completely true. Janine will tell you and Lori will tell you.

One day I had to pump gas — it was a few years ago. They needed my ZIP code, and I panicked. I didn’t know my ZIP code. I don’t know my telephone number. I forget these things. I can live with it.

So Huang is not the only person making these kinds of strange statements. Marc Andreessen proudly declaring not to have any introspection. Sam Altman talking about how how ChatGPT (and probably a bunch of nannies) basically raises his kid. Satya Nadella “staying informed” about the world by listening to – and talking to – podcasts that Microsoft Copilot generates for him.

This is not how actual people live. These are – for actual human beings – very embarrassing things to admit. Why would techbros do that? Constantly.

It of course brings to mind the famous quote from William Gibson’s Count Zero:

“And, for an instant, she stared directly into those soft blue eyes and knew, with an instinctive mammalian certainty, that the exceedingly rich were no longer even remotely human.”

And that is true to a degree: That level of access to money does shift how you see, how you interact with the world. It starts with you having a driver so you never have to park a car or go to the gas/charging station and only increases the more money you have. I would honestly not be surprised if those rich people wouldn’t even know where the washing machine is in their mansion. That’s what the help takes care of.

Money – like software – creates abstraction. Distance to the friction of the world. The ability to never be touched and to never have to touch anyone or anything. To have nobody else’s life, their existence as a person with needs and rights and hopes and feelings, matter. That probably is why rich folks – and those how aspire to that lifestyle – love “AI” so much.

But I think there is another aspect to those statements. They are a test.

Donald Trump (I think more subconsciously than intentionally) is a master of this kind of test. It goes like this: You state something outrageous for example “Lake Ontario is now called Lake America”. People should laugh at you because that is absurd. But some people will instantly call it Lake America (like Google changing what Google Maps says). Those are the people who have passed the test. They have debased themselves in public by following something completely off the rails marking themselves as obedient to the person who started the whole thing.

This is a typical kind of behavior you see in cults or for example right wing extremist groups: If you get people to tattoo a visible swastika on themselves they have not only declared their submission to the group but marked themselves as no longer part of the rest of society.

Everything we say has multiple functions and effects. I am not saying that Jensen Huang intentionally plants these weird-ass statements to test the people around him. I am saying that they do serve as a test though. Because in that interview, Klein could have pushed back on Huang. Really dug into how “I don’t know my address” is not about “some skills are no longer required” but about “I am rich and pay a bunch of women to run my life like my mother used to“. Could have challenged that completely disconnected statement to kinda force Huang to step down from abstraction land down to the real world.

But he didn’t. Because he knows the consequences. If you do challenge those things you will not get those kinds of high-profile interviews. If you don’t take whatever those weird men say seriously you have failed the test. And that has consequences.

It is imperative for us to push back on that. Now we don’t get to talk to Jensen Huang – which might be good for our intellectual and psychological well-being – but we talk to people who might accept those statements and argue based on that. “Jensen Huang said that we don’t need those skills”, “Sam Altman said that Intelligence is something that we can just rent from OpenAI”, “Dario Amodei said AI might kill is all”. Weird and dumb shit that needs to be challenged.

We can’t save those broken men from themselves. We have way bigger tasks in front of us. One of those tasks is pushing back on those claims, pointing out how fucking weird those statements are, how they do not make any lick of sense.

Pointing that out, making that explicit, choosing to fail the test is powerful. It does give others the opportunity to step out of the often dominant “quirky tech bro is so visionary” narrative to realize how fucking weird those guys are. How little they know about life. About how to be a human. And that is power. That is connection. That is what allows us to push back on our lives, our social fabric being steamrolled by a bunch of unpleasant dudes.

The only way to actually win at that test is to fail it. Fail it as hard as you can.

Very well argued. We’ve lived for decades now with crazy stuff from the tech bros that went unchallenged while the media built them up to be Wunderkinder. Like you, I called them out, regularly, for the simple reason that their products tended to be half-baked, the sort of quality you would expect from leaders who had nothing but contempt for their users. Sadly this sycophancy has led us here, when we, as a society, should have called them out from the very beginning.

I’ll never forget once when I was in Aspen (as a journalist, getting free accommodation), and having the sudden flash of realisation as I chatted to a woman in my hotel lobby about her cute dog, that she didn’t see me as a person. Her eyes were completely dead and disengaged. She was giving me the same degree of attention that I, it dawned on me shamefully, might give the guy at the petrol station or the local convenience store, ie, the bare minimum.

When you’re that rich, I think, you just don’t see most people as actual people that you need to think about in any way. Billionaires are not like us.

I had a flatmate from apartheid South Africa. When there she had no idea how tennis shoes are cleaned; she just left them outside her door at night and in the morning they were clean. To her credit, she became an anti-apartheid activist.

I just saw “The Taming of the Shrew” at the Oregon Shakespeare Festival last night, so the scene where Petruchio forces Kate to prove her submission to him by agreeing with him that the sun was actually the moon is fresh in my mind. OSF, with their customary skill and top-notch acting, managed to find a way to make this scene less hideously misogynistic than it actually is — this is always a huge challenge with “Shrew” — but it’s basically the same idea as “the test.”

topStories.fullTranslation:
英伟达（NVIDIA）CEO、世界上最具“中年危机感”皮夹克的拥趸黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）最近上了埃兹拉·克莱恩（Ezra Klein）的播客。说实话，我其实不想让大家去受罪听/读那期节目的全部录音或文字稿。太痛苦了。听着那期节目，你每过一分钟都会感觉自己的心智能力在衰退……有点像在使用聊天机器人，但感觉更糟。

黄仁勋在播客中说了许多荒谬绝伦的话。比如当克莱恩问起孩子们使用大语言模型（LLM）从而学不到技能的问题时，黄仁勋回答道：
“我完全赞同。你现在让一个孩子去做长除法试试看。九九乘法表都快被忘光了。算平方根？天哪。基础数学正在被遗忘。但这重要吗？[…] 是的。我觉得并不重要。我觉得无关紧要。”

极其离谱。但他还要继续往下说，抛出一句更过分的话来“超越”前一句：
“有很多技能根本无关紧要。我先承认一件事，我其实根本不知道自己家住哪。 […] 绝对属实。珍妮（Janine）会告诉你，洛里（Lori）也会告诉你。
有一天我得去加油——那是几年前的事了。加油机需要输邮政编码，我当时就慌了。我不知道自己的邮编。我也不知道自己的电话号码。我老忘这些事情。但我照样过得好好的。”

黄仁勋并不是唯一一个发表此类诡异言论的人。马克·安德森（Marc Andreessen）曾自豪地宣称自己从不内省。萨姆·奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）大谈 ChatGPT（外加大概一群保姆）基本上是如何帮他抚养孩子的。萨提亚·纳德拉（Satya Nadella）则是通过收听并“对话”微软 Copilot 为他生成的播客来“了解世界动态”。

真实的人类根本不是这样生活的。对于一个真正的普通人来说，承认这些事情是非常尴尬的。为什么科技大佬们（techbros）会这么做？而且是屡见不鲜。

这自然让人联想到威廉·吉布森（William Gibson）在《零伯爵》（Count Zero）中的那句名言：
“刹那间，她直勾勾地盯着那双柔和的蓝眼睛，凭借哺乳动物的本能确信无疑：极度富有的人，早已不再具有哪怕一丁点儿的人性。”

在某种程度上，事实确是如此：当你坐拥那般财富时，你看待世界和与世界互动的方式都会发生改变。刚开始，你有了司机，再也不用自己停车或去加油站/充电站；随着财富的增加，这种脱离现实的程度只会愈演愈烈。说实话，如果那些富豪连自己豪宅里的洗衣机在哪都不知道，我也一点不会感到意外。反正有下人打理。

金钱——就像软件一样——创造了抽象层。隔绝了现实世界的摩擦与繁琐。赋予了你永远不被任何人或任何事触碰、也永远不必触碰任何人或任何事的能力。让别人的生活，让他们作为拥有需求、权利、希望和情感的个体的存在，变得无足轻重。这或许就是为什么富人们——以及那些渴望这种生活方式的人——如此钟爱“人工智能”（AI）。

但我认为，这些言论背后还有另一个层面。它们是一场“考验”（test）。

唐纳德·特朗普（我认为更多是出于潜意识而非刻意为之）是这种考验的大师。流程是这样的：你抛出一个荒谬透顶的说法，比如“安大略湖现在改叫美国湖了”。人们本该嘲笑你，因为这简直荒谬至极。但有些人会立刻改口叫它“美国湖”（就像谷歌会去修改谷歌地图上的标注一样）。这些人就是通过了考验的人。他们通过盲从这种彻头彻尾的荒唐言论，在公众面前自我贬低，以此标明自己对挑起事端者的顺从。

这是一种在邪教或极右翼极端组织中常见的典型行为：如果你能让人们在身上刺上醒目的纳粹卐字符号，他们不仅宣示了对该组织的臣服，更标明了自己已不再属于社会主流群体。

我们所说的每一句话都具有多重功能与效应。我并不是说黄仁勋是故意抛出这些古怪离奇的言论来测试身边的人。但我是说，这些言论确实起到了考验的作用。因为在那场采访中，克莱恩本可以反驳黄仁勋，真正去深究“我不知道我的住址”根本不是什么“有些技能已不再需要”，而是“我很有钱，花钱雇了一群女人像我妈当年那样照料我的生活”。他本可以去质疑这种完全脱节的言论，在某种程度上逼迫黄仁勋从抽象的神坛跌落回现实世界。

但他并没有这么做。因为他深知其后果。如果你真去质疑那些事，你就拿不到这种重量级的大牌访谈了。如果你不把这些怪人说的任何话当回事，你就没有通过考验。而这会带来代价。

我们必须对此进行反击。虽然我们没机会去和黄仁勋当面辩论——这或许对我们的智识和心理健康也是件好事——但我们会接触到那些可能会采纳这些言论并以此为据进行争辩的人。“黄仁勋说了，我们不需要那些技能”、“萨姆·奥尔特曼说了，智能不过是我们能向 OpenAI 租用的一种东西”、“达里奥·阿莫代（Dario Amodei）说 AI 可能会杀死我们所有人”。全都是荒唐透顶的废话，必须予以痛击。

我们无法把这些心理残缺的人从他们自身的泥潭中拯救出来。摆在我们面前的任务要宏大得多。其中一项任务就是对这些论调进行反击，指出这些言论到底有多么荒谬绝伦，它们根本就狗屁不通。

把这点指出来，挑明它，选择在考验中“交白卷不及格”，是极具力量的。它确实能给其他人提供一个跳出主流的“古怪科技大佬极具远见”叙事框架的机会，去认清这些家伙究竟有多么诡异。去认清他们对生活一无所知，对如何做一个正常人一无所知。这就是力量。这就是连接。正是这种力量，让我们能够奋起反抗，不让我们的生活和社会肌理被这群令人讨厌的家伙肆意碾碎。

真正通过这场考验的唯一方式，就是让自己通不过。尽可能彻底地交出不及格的答卷。

论证得非常精彩。几十年来，我们一直面对着科技大佬们的疯狂胡言乱语而无人质疑，与此同时媒体却把他们捧成了神童（Wunderkinder）。和你一样，我也经常揭露他们，原因很简单：他们的产品往往半生不熟，正是那种对用户充斥着蔑视的掌舵者才会拿出的品质。可悲的是，这种阿谀奉承将我们引向了当下的境地，而我们全社会本应从一开始就站出来揭穿他们。

我永远不会忘记有一次在阿斯彭（当时作为记者获得了免费住宿），当我在酒店大堂和一位女士聊起她可爱的小狗时，我猛然意识到：她根本没有把我当成一个人来看待。她的眼神完全是空洞而漠然的。我羞愧地意识到，她对我的注意程度，就像我对待加油站或当地便利店店员那样——也就是维持在最低限度。

我认为，当你富裕到那种程度时，你根本不会把大多数人当成需要你在意或考虑的真正的人。亿万富翁和我们截然不同。

我曾有一位来自种族隔离时期的南非室友。在南非生活时，她完全不知道网球鞋是怎么洗干净的；她只需要在晚上把鞋放在门外，早晨鞋子就已经被清洗干净了。值得称赞的是，她后来成为了一名反种族隔离活动人士。

昨晚我刚在俄勒冈莎士比亚戏剧节（OSF）观看了《驯悍记》，因此佩特鲁乔强迫凯特通过认同“太阳其实是月亮”来证明对他的顺从这一幕，在我脑海中依然历历在目。俄勒冈莎士比亚戏剧节凭借其一贯的高超技巧和顶尖演技，想方设法让这一幕显得没有原本那么严重而丑陋的厌女色彩——这在《驯悍记》中始终是个巨大的挑战——但这与“测试”的逻辑基本上如出一辙。

topStories.title: 我厌倦了身处网络之中
topStories.originalTitle: I'm Tired of Being on the Network
topStories.fullContent:
You can tell how tired someone is of the always-online life pretty easily. When they get home, watch the distance between the phone and the body. The people who love being connected never let the thing leave them be it pocket, palm, face-down next to the fork. Everyone else sets it down the way you drop a heavy backpack after a long day of walking. My wife does not set her phone down so much as launch it. From her hand to the far corner of the room, the phone travels from indispensable to litter in under a second.

For my part, I've come to resent the smartphone, which is an embarrassing thing to admit, because I used to be a believer. I researched every new model. I switched between iOS and Android just to taste each new future as it arrived. I lined up for the first iPhone at 3 a.m., stood in the dark to get a glimpse of the thing itself. I remember being genuinely moved when the Apple Store employees clapped for me. In hindsight this is mortifying, roughly on par with the year I dyed my hair blonde and shopped at Hot Topic. We used to have passionate arguments about whether iOS or Android was the future. Sitting here right now, I cannot tell you which model of iPhone is in my pocket. I can't name a single reason I'd upgrade, except that eventually the battery dies, and I don't feel like swapping it myself. Again.

It was a dream, for a while: internet everywhere, always. Star Trek made real. I could send an email from a country road. I could read a webpage from a bathroom, which, fine, is where a lot of it belonged. My first computer had no networking at all, and then: dial-up, ethernet, wireless, the phone in my pocket. Each step felt like proof that the future arrived on schedule. These were prized possessions. You cherished them. You had feelings about the merits of one versus another.

Now the smartphone is a tax. I get to choose my tax collector be it Apple, Samsung, Google, Nothing, Fairphone, but I don't get to choose whether to pay. In Denmark I'm expected to carry the Aula app for school, the Rejsekort app for trains, MitID to prove to the state that I am me, and e-Boks for official messages from the government and its authorized friends. I need the thing at the airport, at the hotel, at the gym. All of this, I'm told, is a choice. I "choose" to take part in the digital economy.

It isn't a choice in any meaningful sense. It's compliance. It's the one physical counter open Tuesdays from 10 to 12, and the ticket machine that no longer takes cash. And the offline option exists the way the wheelchair ramp exists at certain train stations: installed after the fact, satisfying a regulation, pitched at an angle no wheelchair on earth can climb. We are all expected to pretend grandma can make it up, and to act only mildly surprised when we find her at the bottom again.

So every few years I buy the identical slab of metal and glass. I admire the color for a moment, because color is the only decision left to make. The last honest pleasure in a new phone is peeling the plastic film off the screen after which the box contains nothing of interest. I put the slab in a case so durable I never see the color again, restore from backup, and everything the old slab knew migrates, whole and continuous, into the new one. A soul transfer, over Wi-Fi, in ninety seconds. I feel nothing for the old slab, despite years of daily intimacy. I hand it off or sell it and never think of it again.

I understood something had gone wrong in me the first time I dropped the phone and didn't mind. I was standing in my living room, mid-negotiation of a play date over WhatsApp, when an email arrived from my mother and a calendar alert reminded me I'd never scheduled the dog's vet appointment. It was as if the phone simply left my hands on its own. It hit the floor with that specific thonk of expensive object meeting laminate. When I picked it up and saw that the screen had survived, I was a tiny bit sad.

After that, I couldn't stop seeing everything I hated about the thing. It was like the last months of a relationship, when everything the other person does induces fury. Why am I out of storage? I don't control the size of the apps that install themselves, or whether my photos are kept at full resolution or quietly compressed into nothing. I'm not allowed to control any part of the experience, so I don't consider the disk space my fucking problem.

Apple pings me, yet again, about my three complimentary months of Apple Music. I open the App Store and find an endless sea of garbage with ads floating on top of the garbage, developers screaming for attention on the burning trash river that is the iOS App Store in 2026. My maps have ads. My apps have ads. Many of the ads are for installing more apps. My podcast app shows me an ad for a podcast about digital detox.

I have come to actively hate this rectangle of annoyances. It is a rectangle I carry from room to room and charge every night so it can go on notifying me, on behalf of applications I was forced to install, because somebody's OKR that quarter was "increase app installs by 15 percent." I don't need to know about the AliExpress sale. There is always an AliExpress sale.

To keep from subconsciously smashing the current slab and having to buy its successor, I started leaving the phone by the front door, next to where I stack the garbage. But the fatigue found me anyway. I'd sit down to play something and get hit with a dozen download prompts. The Steam Deck is always downloading something, or trying to. Streaming has ads now, or else the show has quietly gone missing. My wife and I say insane things to each other, like, "Which app had the show from last week?" HBO counts it off — "ad one of seven" — then detonates sports-betting commercials at maximum volume, until whatever fragile interest I had in the show dies of exposure.

There is an incredible sameness to all of it. Everyone online speaks in the same broken loop of the same ten phrases. Every streaming show (except, weirdly, Apple TV+, and who called that) is written as though I'm the stupidest person alive, plot beats arriving on schedule, like a waiter screaming the order at a customer with a head injury who has already nodded twice. Emily in Paris is on: the story of an American woman trapped in a Parisian time loop. She's with the French chef. Now she isn't. Now she is again. Different dress. Compared to what's arrived since, poor Emily is Shakespeare.

The snake has begun eating itself. Netflix has shows about TikTok stars running their social-media empires. HBO has a murder documentary where most of the commentary is social-media clips of people theorizing about the murder. It's a closed loop. Soon we'll produce the documentary while the original event is still happening.

Whatever hope I had for the internet is long dead, and I've made a shaky peace with most of what killed it. We persist anyway because I can't retire and wouldn't have anything to do if I did.

For me: a bare circuit board. I still like playing with tech, I just need something contained. I need something where I can just engage with something that doesn't involve a million hooks and attempts to get me to do something else.

The end result looks like this (not my actual unit — I dropped it and cracked the plastic so: imagine this, but worse):

The first game I loaded was Crash Bandicoot for the PlayStation. When I played it as a kid, it was a technical marvel. It is hard to overstate how Crash looked and felt, coming from the Genesis and the NES. PS1 games in general have a soothing grammar, because they assume nothing. They know you rented this from a Blockbuster on a Friday night, that the manual is missing, and that you need to understand the game inside of thirty seconds.

Each Crash level introduces exactly one new thing, shows it to you up front in a low-stakes loop, and lets you figure it out. It starts easy. Then the mechanics stack, and stack, until the jumps demand something close to pixel-perfect, and I notice I'm leaning forward on the couch, fully dialed in to the triangle-headed marsupial.

It puts me back in the arcade at the mall a town over from my house. My dad would drop me off at the Defiance mall, which had a small arcade near the movie theater, across from the Chinese food stand in the food court. We'd line up in the dark for a shot at one of the Street Fighter II machines, quarters stacked on the bezel to call the next game. The carpet was always weirdly sticky. The joysticks were still sweaty from the last failed challenger. The mechanics of that era were simple, but you had to execute them perfectly, in public.

After a few hours I take a break. I pause the game and leave the box running, and hours later I come back to find everything exactly where I left it. No session expired. Nothing has decided I need to log in again. It just keeps humming, the little fan I installed purring away. It exists to keep doing the thing I asked it to do, and it has no other ambitions.

When we first got computers, this is simply what they were. By default they did nothing. They sat there and waited for you to have an idea. My old Macintosh LC II would basically wait around for inspiration to strike, or for me to waste an afternoon opening and closing folders, because software was expensive and folder-clicking was free. They felt like tools, not toys, and (ironically) the reason we knew how to do anything on them was that we spent hours poking around System 7, figuring out where everything lived. They crashed. Often, if we're being honest. But nothing in that machine wanted anything from me.

Is the MiSTer perfect? No. It's a board engineers test things on, and the software is flawed in exactly the ways you'd expect software like this to be flawed. The UI is clunky, pairing your first controller sorta sucks, and at no point has anyone optimized my experience. But it exists not as the physical manifestation of some roadmap I'll be subjected to later, but as a snapshot of a thing that exists on its own terms. Like the LC II, it's a thing designed to do a thing. It sits there with wires dangling out of it, doing exactly that.

It asks nothing of me. It knows nothing about me.
topStories.fullTranslation:
一个人有多厌倦这种“时刻在线”的生活，很容易就能看出来。当他们回到家时，观察一下手机与身体之间的距离便一目了然。那些热爱与网络保持连接的人，永远不会让这玩意儿离开自己——无论是在口袋里、手掌中，还是扣在叉子旁。其他人放下手机的方式，就像徒步跋涉了一整天后卸下沉重的双肩包一样。至于我妻子，与其说是放下手机，不如说是把手机“发射”出去。从她的手中到房间的远角，手机在不到一秒的时间里，就从不可或缺的必需品沦为了杂物垃圾。

就我而言，我已经开始厌恶智能手机了。承认这一点让我感到有些难堪，因为我曾经也是个坚定的信徒。我曾研究过每一款新机型。我曾不断在 iOS 和 Android 之间切换，只为在每一个新未来到来之时抢先尝鲜。我曾在凌晨 3 点排队购买第一代 iPhone，在黑暗中伫立，只为亲眼目睹这台设备的真容。我甚至还记得当年 Apple Store 员工为我鼓掌时，我内心由衷的感动。如今回想起来，这简直令人无地自容，大约等同于我当年把头发染成金黄色、跑去 Hot Topic 服装店扫货的那一年。我们曾经就 iOS 和 Android 究竟谁代表未来展开过激烈的辩论。而此时此刻坐在这里，我甚至说不出自己口袋里装的是哪一代 iPhone。我也找不出哪怕一个换机的理由，除了电池最终老化耗尽，而我又不想再自己动手换一次电池了。

曾经有段时间，这是一个梦想：随时随地连接互联网。《星际迷航》照进了现实。我可以在乡间小路上发送电子邮件。我可以坐在马桶上看网页——好吧，网上很多垃圾内容原本就该归入马桶。我的第一台电脑完全没有联网功能，紧接着：拨号上网、以太网、无线网络，再到口袋里的手机。每一步都像是证明未来正准时赴约的铁证。这些曾是我们珍视的宝贝。你对它们悉心呵护。你对这个产品相比另一个的优劣有着真实的情感倾注。

如今，智能手机却成了一种税。我可以选择我的收税官——无论是苹果、三星、谷歌、Nothing 还是 Fairphone——但我无法选择交不交税。在丹麦，我必须装用于学校事务的 Aula 应用、用于乘坐火车的 Rejsekort 应用、用于向国家证明“我是我”的 MitID，以及用于接收政府及其授权机构官方信函的 e-Boks。我在机场需要它，在酒店需要它，在健身房也需要它。所有这一切，别人却告诉我这是一种选择——是我“选择”参与数字经济。

在任何有实际意义的层面，这都不是一种选择。这是顺从。这就像每周二上午 10 点到 12 点才开放一次的唯一实体柜台，以及不再接收现金的售票机。而“离线”这一选项的存在方式，就像某些火车站里的轮椅坡道：事后补建，为了满足监管规定，但坡度陡峭到地球上没有任何轮椅能够爬得上去。可我们所有人都被要求假装老奶奶能自己滑上去，并在发现她又跌落到底部时，只表现出一丝温和的惊讶。

于是，每隔几年我就会买下一块一模一样的金属与玻璃板砖。我会花上一瞬间欣赏一下它的颜色，因为颜色是如今唯一还留给用户做决定的东西。新手机能带来的最后一点纯粹的快乐，就是撕掉屏幕上的塑料保护膜——此后，包装盒里就再也没有任何能引起兴趣的东西了。我把这块板砖套进一个结实耐用以至于我再也看不见其机身颜色的保护壳里，从备份中恢复数据，于是旧板砖所知道的一切，便完整而连贯地迁移到了新板砖中。一场通过 Wi-Fi 在 90 秒内完成的灵魂转移。尽管朝夕相处了数年，我对旧板砖却毫无留恋。我把它送人或卖掉，从此再也不会想起它。

第一次摔了手机却毫不在意时，我意识到自己内心有些东西出了问题。当时我正站在客厅里，一边通过 WhatsApp 商量孩子的聚会时间，一边收到了母亲发来的邮件，日历提醒又在此刻通知我一直忘了给狗狗预约看兽医。那一刻，手机就像是自己从我手中脱落了一样。它摔在地板上，发出昂贵物体撞击复合地板时特有的钝响。当我捡起手机发现屏幕完好无损时，心里竟然闪过一丝淡淡的失落。

从那以后，我眼里全是对这玩意儿的厌恶。这就好比一段关系走向终结的最后几个月，对方的一举一动都能引发你的滔天怒火。为什么我的存储空间又满了？擅自安装的应用体积有多大不受我控制，我的照片是被保留原始分辨率还是被悄悄压缩得模糊不清也不受我控制。既然我被剥夺了对体验任何细节的控制权，那存储空间不够用就他妈不关我的事。

苹果又一次向我推送提示，催我领取那三个月的 Apple Music 免费试用。我打开 App Store，看到的是无边无际的垃圾海洋，垃圾上方漂浮着广告，在 2026 年宛如一条燃烧的垃圾河般的 iOS App Store 里，开发者们歇斯底里地争夺着用户的注意力。我的地图里有广告。我的应用里有广告。其中许多广告还是为了诱导你安装更多应用。就连我的播客应用都在向我推送一档关于“数字排毒”的播客广告。

我已经开始打心底里憎恶这个令人烦躁的长方形物件。我把它从一个房间带到另一个房间，每天晚上给它充电，好让它能代表那些我被迫安装的应用继续向我轰炸通知，只因为某人那一季度的 OKR 目标是“应用安装量提升 15%”。我根本不需要知道速卖通（AliExpress）又在打折。速卖通永远都在打折。

为了防止潜意识里砸烂手头这块板砖而不得不去买个替代品，我开始把手机留在前门边，就堆在我放垃圾的地方旁边。但那种疲惫感还是如影随形。我坐下来想玩点什么，迎面而来的却是十几个下载提示。Steam Deck 永远在下载某些东西，或者正试图下载。流媒体现在充斥着广告，要么就是某些节目已经悄无声息地下架了。我和妻子常常会对彼此说一些匪夷所思的话，比如：“上周看的那部剧在哪个 App 里来着？”HBO 会倒数计时——“第 1 条广告，共 7 条”——然后以最大音量轰炸体育博彩广告，直到我对那部剧仅存的一点脆弱兴趣被彻底磨灭殆尽。

这一切呈现出一种令人难以置信的千篇一律。网络上的每个人都在重复着由相同的十句话构成的破烂死循环。每一部流媒体剧集（奇怪的是 Apple TV+ 除外，谁能料到呢）的编剧水平都仿佛把观众当成了全天下最蠢的人，剧情节拍准时到来，就像服务员对着已经点头确认过两次的脑损伤顾客歇斯底里地大吼菜单。《艾米丽在巴黎》（Emily in Paris）正在播出：一个困在巴黎时间循环里的美国女人的故事。她和法国主厨在一起了。现在分了。现在又在一起了。换了身裙子。跟后来出现的那些作品相比，可怜的艾米丽简直称得上是莎士比亚。

这条蛇已经开始吞食自己的尾巴。Netflix 上出现了关于 TikTok 网红运营其社交媒体帝国的节目。HBO 则有一部谋杀案纪录片，其中大部分解说竟然是人们在社交媒体上对该谋杀案进行理论推演的视频剪辑。这是一个闭环。很快，我们就会在原始事件还在发生的同时，就已经把纪录片制作出来了。

我曾对互联网抱有的任何希望早已彻底破灭，而对于扼杀它的绝大多数元凶，我也已经达成了脆弱的和解。我们依然在苟延残喘，只因为我还不能退休，即便退休了我也无事可做。

对我而言：一块裸露的电路板。我依然喜欢摆弄科技产品，只是需要一些封闭自足的东西。我需要的是这样一种载体：我可以沉浸其中，而不需要面对数以百万计的挂钩以及诱导我去做其他事情的企图。

最终的成果看起来就像这样（不是我实际使用的那一台——我把它摔了，塑料外壳摔裂了，所以想象一下这个画面，但情况更糟）：

我加载的第一款游戏是 PlayStation 上的《古惑狼》（Crash Bandicoot）。小时候玩它时，它堪称技术奇迹。从世嘉五代（Genesis）和红白机（NES）时代走过来，你很难用言语夸大《古惑狼》在视觉与触感上带来的震撼。整体而言，PS1 游戏有一种让人安心的逻辑，因为它们不作任何预设。它们知道你是在周五晚上从百视达（Blockbuster）租来的这张光盘，说明书已经丢了，而且你必须在三十秒内弄懂怎么玩。

《古惑狼》的每一关都只引入一个新机制，并以低风险的循环方式直接展示给你，让你自己琢磨明白。它始于简单。随后机制层层叠加，直到跳跃操作要求近乎像素级的精准，我发现自己正坐在沙发上前倾着身子，全神贯注于那只三角形脑袋的有袋类动物。

这让我重回离我家隔壁小镇商场里的街机厅。我父亲会把我送到迪法恩斯（Defiance）商场，电影院附近有一家小街机厅，就在美食广场的中餐摊位对面。我们在黑暗中排队等待在某台《街头霸王 II》（Street Fighter II）街机上大战一把，硬币叠放在机身屏幕边框上表示排队占机。地毯总是莫名其妙地黏糊糊的。摇杆上还残留着上一位落败挑战者的汗水。那个时代的机制很简单，但你必须当着众人的面，将操作发挥得完美无缺。

几个小时后，我休息了一下。我暂停了游戏，让机子继续运行；几小时后再回来，发现所有东西依然停留在离开时的状态。会话没有超时。没有任何机制判定我需要重新登录。它只是继续低鸣，我安装的小风扇在嗡嗡作响。它存在只是为了继续做我要求它做的事情，别无其他企图。

当我们最初拥有计算机时，它们本来就是这个样子的。默认情况下它们什么也不做。它们静静地坐在那里，等待你产生一个想法。我的旧款 Macintosh LC II 基本上就是在等待灵感降临，或是等我浪费一个下午在不断打开和关闭文件夹上，因为软件很昂贵，而点点文件夹是免费的。它们感觉像是工具，而不是玩具；而且（具讽刺意味的是）我们之所以知道如何在它们上面操作，是因为我们花了数小时在 System 7 中到处乱试，弄清楚每样东西都在哪里。它们会崩溃。坦白讲，崩溃挺频繁的。但那台机器里没有任何东西试图从我这里索取任何东西。

MiSTer 是完美的吗？不。它是一块供工程师测试东西的板子，软件存在的缺陷也正是你预料之中的那种软件缺陷。界面笨拙，第一次配对控制器体验很糟，而且从来没有任何人为我优化过体验。但它的存在并不是为了体现我日后不得不顺从的某种产品路线图，而是作为一种按自身规律存在的客观事物的定格。就像 LC II 一样，它就是为了完成某件事而被设计出来的东西。它静静地立在那里，电线在外面垂挂着，兢兢业业地做着那件事。

它不向我索取任何东西。它对我一无所知。

topStories.title: Insta360征服了全景相机领域——如今它正瞄准智能眼镜
topStories.originalTitle: Insta360 conquered 360 cameras — now it’s eyeing glasses

topStories.fullContent: It’s right there in the name: “Insta360” makes 360-degree cameras, ones that film every angle simultaneously so you can shoot first and frame later. It didn’t invent the idea, but Insta360 has become so synonymous with 360 cameras that it dominates the category with 73 percent of worldwide marketshare. It’s preparing to ship so many cameras, it just spent $298 million — more than GoPro’s entire valuation — on memory chips alone. But as Insta360 sells its 10 millionth camera and opens its first flagship US store in New York City’s Times Square, it’s thinking bigger than two hemispherical lenses on a stick. It’s looking to challenge Canon, Sony, Nikon, and Fujifilm by becoming a “top imaging camera company” or “even a tech company,” cofounder Max Richter tells me — and it’s experimentally building its own mirrorless cameras and smart glasses to get there. Insta360, also known as Shadow Stone or Arashi Vision in its native China, isn’t targeting Meta’s AI glasses or DSLR-wielding professional photographers just yet. Nor is it trying to replace the smartphone camera in your pocket. [Image: The Insta360 X6, on a selfie stick. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/insta360_x6_2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] “We don’t try to fight against the rise of the smartphone in photography and content creation,” says Richter. “We see that there’s an opportunity between smartphone users and professional cameras — a growing trend that people want to express themselves,” he adds. He tells me that if Insta360 were to sell a pair of smart glasses, “we wouldn’t necessarily compete with companies on smart intelligent features.” It’d be about helping people conveniently capture high-quality images, not about an AI assistant on your face. And while that doesn’t sidestep the “pervert glasses” problem, there might be room for Insta360 to go about it differently, with headgear that’s obviously a camera instead of covertly spying. Though Insta360’s smart glasses ambitions haven’t been widely reported — I could only find one brief mention — founder JK Liu previously confirmed that two mirrorless cameras are already in development. One will have a shape that “you have never thought of before,” Liu told MyNavi News in August. (Liu reportedly became a billionaire when Insta360 went public last year.) “When you think about mirrorless, for us it would really go into making it more convenient and making a camera that is really suited for a new generation of content creators, not necessarily what’s already out there on the market,” Richter tells The Verge. If Insta360 does expand into those camera categories, they’ll just be the tip of the spear. The company has already been pushing into many other categories dominated by its Chinese rival DJI, including DJI-challenging drones, gimbals and gimbaled baby steadycams, and modular action cameras. [Image: Insta360’s current camera lineup, not counting its drone and professional VR rigs. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/insta360-camera-lineup.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] While Insta360 might be the 360-camera market leader with 73 percent share, it’s a distant number 2 in other categories that DJI serves. IDC estimates that Insta360 has 20 percent of the worldwide handheld smart camera market compared to DJI’s 73 percent overall. Still, Insta360 is making significant headway: In Q2 2026, it had 43 percent of the detachable action camera market, 17 percent of non-detachable GoPro style action cameras, and its brand-new Luna Ultra already has 6 percent marketshare in gimbaled cameras. GoPro itself, meanwhile, is a distant number 3 in IDC data, with just 3 percent of the smart camera market in Q2 2026, after shipments fell by half to just 200,000 cameras in the quarter. It’s not unthinkable that Insta360 could help challenge traditional cameras. The traditional market leader, Canon, shipped 4.5 million digital cameras last year according to Nikkei data. DJI shipped 4.3 million cameras last quarter alone, according to IDC. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/INSTA360s-1_9625ad.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/INSTA360-5.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Insta360’s founders have explained that their grand vision is to become the robot cameraman for the world — not necessarily an actual humanoid robot, but rather an expectation that these devices can do more and more of the capture and motion and editing themselves, automatically understanding your intent using built-in AI tech. The company’s latest Insta360 X6 is another small step in this direction: It comes with an onboard AI model and enough processing to automatically create a highlight reel from your footage while the camera is plugged in and charging, and it’s got a 2.0 version of a previous “InstaFrame” feature that can track and frame the person you select and automatically produce a video. Insta360’s also launching a new feature for the X6 that can create 3D Gaussian splats with one tap in the company’s smartphone app, for free. It takes an hour or two for cloud servers to process the video, and users will only get four free splats per month, says Insta360 spokesperson Caroline Chen, but early results look neat. It’s not at all clear whether the United States will embrace Insta360 the way Insta360 has embraced the US. While Apple, Best Buy, and Costco all stock the company’s products, that could change if the US government decides to enact a foreign camera ban — or if it simply decides that Insta360 is a drone company, like DJI, and pushes back on its cameras, too. [Image: Insta360 technically already has a headset — it comes with the Antigravity A1 drone. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/08/20250701_150141.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Insta360 already distanced itself from its drone brand Antigravity in the lead-up to the US drone ban, which will theoretically prevent Antigravity from shipping any future drones into the United States. Its first drone beat the ban by weeks. As for Insta360, “We remain on the ground,” Richter tells me. “When it comes to drones, it’s not something that Insta360 is working on,” he says, suggesting I speak to Antigravity CEO Michael Shabun instead. Richter says he’s “quite confident” that he can continue to bring cameras to people all around the world, and that Insta360 will fully comply with any local laws, but admits “there are certain things that are out of our control.” I ask: Would Insta360 consider hedging against future risk by manufacturing some products in the US? If the company was required to, perhaps — but there’s no current plan to do so. “We would potentially look into it, but it’s not in our plan or roadmap at this moment.” He says the US is a key market, and Insta360 plans to be there for the long haul.
topStories.fullTranslation:
名字本身就说明了一切：“Insta360”制造360度全景相机，这种相机能同时拍摄各个角度，让你能够先拍摄后取景。这一构想并非由它发明，但Insta360如今已几乎成为全景相机的代名词，在全球占据了该品类73%的市场份额。它正准备大量出货相机，仅在存储芯片上的支出就高达2.98亿美元——这超过了GoPro的整体估值。然而，随着Insta360卖出其第1000万台相机并在纽约时代广场开设其首家美国旗舰店，其雄心已远不止于一根自拍杆上的两个半球形镜头。联合创始人马克斯·里希特（Max Richter）告诉我，该公司正寻求通过成为一家“顶级影像相机公司”或“甚至是科技公司”，来向佳能、索尼、尼康和富士发起挑战——为了实现这一目标，它正通过实验性研发自有的无反相机和智能眼镜来进行探索。

在其本土中国被称为“影石”（Shadow Stone 或 Arashi Vision）的Insta360，目前尚不打算直接与Meta的AI眼镜竞争，也不针对手持单反相机的专业摄影师。它同样没有试图取代你口袋里的智能手机摄像头。

[图片：安装在自拍杆上的Insta360 X6。https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/insta360_x6_2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

“我们并不打算对抗智能手机在摄影和内容创作领域的崛起，”里希特表示。“我们看到智能手机用户与专业相机之间存在着机遇——人们表达自我的愿望正日益强烈，”他补充道。

他告诉我，如果Insta360推出一款智能眼镜，“我们不一定会和各家公司在智能算法功能上竞争。”它的核心在于帮助人们便捷地捕捉高质量画面，而不是在你的脸上安放一个AI助手。虽然这并不能彻底绕开所谓的“偷拍眼镜”（pervert glasses）隐患，但Insta360或许有空间采取不同的方式——打造一款让人一眼就能看出是相机的头戴设备，而不是进行隐秘的窥视。

尽管Insta360在智能眼镜方面的野心尚未被广泛报道——我仅能找到一处简要提及——但创始人刘靖康（JK Liu）此前已证实，有两款无反相机已经在研发中。刘靖康在8月接受MyNavi News采访时表示，其中一款将拥有“你此前从未设想过的”外形。（据报道，刘靖康在Insta360去年上市时已跻身亿万富豪之列。）

“谈到无反相机，对我们而言，重点在于让它变得更加便捷，打造一款真正契合新一代内容创作者的相机，而不必照搬市场上现有的产品形态，”里希特对The Verge表示。

如果Insta360确实进军这些相机细分品类，那也仅仅是其尖兵出击的第一步。该公司已经在积极渗透其中国竞争对手大疆（DJI）所主导的诸多其他领域，包括向大疆发起挑战的无人机、云台及手持小型稳定器，以及模块化运动相机。

[图片：Insta360当前的相机产品线，未计入其无人机和专业级VR设备。https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/insta360-camera-lineup.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

虽然Insta360可能凭借73%的份额雄踞全景相机市场榜首，但在大疆涉足的其他品类中，它仍处于遥遥落后的第二位。据IDC测算，Insta360在全球手持智能相机市场中占据20%的份额，而大疆整体占据73%。即便如此，Insta360仍在取得显著进展：在2026年第二季度，它在分体式运动相机市场占有43%的份额，在GoPro式的一体式运动相机市场占有17%，而其全新的Luna Ultra在云台相机领域已斩获6%的市场份额。与此同时，IDC数据显示，GoPro本身已跌至遥远的第三位，在2026年第二季度的智能相机市场中仅占3%，当季出货量减半至仅20万台。

Insta360有望向传统相机发起挑战并非不可想象。根据《日本经济新闻》的数据，传统市场霸主佳能去年出货了450万台数码相机。而根据IDC的数据，仅上个季度，大疆的出货量就达到了430万台。

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/INSTA360s-1_9625ad.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

[图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/INSTA360-5.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

Insta360的创始人们曾阐述，他们的宏伟愿景是成为“全世界的机器人摄影师”——不一定是真正的人形机器人，而是希望这些设备自身能够承担越来越多的拍摄、运动运镜和剪辑工作，利用内置的AI技术自动理解你的意图。该公司最新的Insta360 X6正是在这个方向上迈出的又一小步：它配备了板载AI模型和充足的处理能力，可以在相机插电充电时自动从拍摄素材中生成高光精彩集锦，同时还配备了此前“InstaFrame”功能的2.0版本，能够自动追踪并框选你指定的人物，并生成一段视频。

Insta360还为X6推出了一项新功能，只需在该公司的智能手机App中轻轻一点，即可免费生成3D高斯泼溅（3D Gaussian splatting）模型。Insta360发言人卡罗琳·陈（Caroline Chen）表示，云端服务器处理视频需要一到两个小时，用户每月只能免费生成4个高斯模型，但初期的成像效果看起来十分惊艳。

目前尚完全无法确定美国是否会像Insta360拥抱美国那样接纳这家公司。尽管苹果、百思买（Best Buy）和好市多（Costco）都在销售该公司的产品，但如果美国政府决定出台针对外国相机的禁令——或者干脆像对待大疆那样将Insta360认定为无人机公司，并对其相机业务进行限制，这种情况就可能发生改变。

[图片：严格来说Insta360已经拥有一款头显设备——它随Antigravity A1无人机附带。https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/08/20250701_150141.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

在美国无人机禁令出台前夕，Insta360已经与其无人机品牌Antigravity拉开了距离，该禁令理论上将阻止Antigravity今后向美国出口任何无人机。其首款无人机赶在禁令生效前数周上市。至于Insta360，“我们立足于地面，”里希特告诉我。“就无人机而言，这不是Insta360正在涉足的项目，”他说，并建议我直接去采访Antigravity首席执行官迈克尔·沙本（Michael Shabun）。

里希特表示，他“相当有信心”能够继续向世界各地的人们供应相机，并且Insta360将全面遵守任何当地法律法规，但他坦言“有些事情非我们所能控制”。我问道：Insta360是否会考虑通过在美国本土生产部分产品来对冲未来风险？如果公司被强制要求这么做，或许会——但目前尚无此类计划。“我们可能会考虑这一选项，但这并不在目前的计划或路线图之中。”他表示，美国是一个关键市场，Insta360计划在这里长期深耕。

topStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The new Copilot merges AI chat, coding, and Autopilot agents.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Tom Warren

After teasing its new Copilot “super app” last month, Microsoft is officially unveiling it today. The redesigned Copilot app bundles three AI capabilities into a single interface of chat, coding, and agents. As part of the launch, Microsoft is also rebranding Scout, the AI personal assistant it unveiled at Build earlier this year, as Autopilot.

This new Copilot app will have three tabs for Home, Code, and Autopilot, with Home combining Copilot Chat and Cowork together. It’s the default landing experience for Copilot users, and Microsoft is also planning to include a Today feature inside it that works as a personalized dashboard for important emails, meeting requests, Teams threads, and more.

“Home is where you get your bearings, keeping you grounded and moving forward: review recent activity, get suggestions on what Copilot can help with, and pick up work right where you left off,” explains Jared Spataro, chief marketing officer of AI at work at Microsoft.

The Code tab is the surprise addition to this so-called “super app,” and not one you’d typically associate with an app designed for knowledge workers. It will let anyone create an app, tracker, dashboard, or automation and share the results with colleagues as cloud-hosted internal apps. “Powered by the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot, Code runs in a sandboxed environment and can be hosted securely within your tenant,” says Spataro.

Autopilot is a new addition to the Copilot experience, and one that Spataro describes as a “digital teammate.” Previously called Scout and available initially as a desktop app, Autopilot is the cloud equivalent that enables a personal AI assistant to keep running while you’re asleep. Like many other AI agents, Autopilot has its own cloud computer instance that can be tasked to do things like watch Teams channels, run recurring work tasks, or handle follow-ups.

The real difference against some other AI agents is that Microsoft has made Autopilot enterprise grade, appealing to businesses that rely on its Office and identity management suites. “Autopilot lives in your tenant with its own identity, memory, computer, and workspace, and it’s built on Microsoft IQ so it understands how your organization actually works,” says Spataro. “It shows up where people already work — Teams, Outlook, chats, channels, and documents — so you can @mention it like a colleague, with permissions, audit, and governance behind it.”

All of this focus on enterprise security and control is a big part of Microsoft trying to sell businesses on Copilot once again. The difference this time around is that how much a business pays for Copilot will depend on what their employees are doing. Microsoft is using usage-based billing for the Cowork, Code, and Autopilot parts of this new Copilot app, so any long-running agentic capabilities or usage of models like Astra and Fable will be billed based on usage.

The regular Copilot license, known as a user subscription license, will give you Copilot in Chat, and in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams. Microsoft is using an auto model picker to match the model for each task, but IT admins will need to use Microsoft’s new FinOps for AI to manage AI spend and ensure any agentic usage doesn’t get out of control.

With this new Copilot app it feels like Microsoft has finally settled on a formula for its AI assistant. The company has redesigned Copilot plenty of times since its introduction as a chatbot inside Bing, and this latest three-tab design builds on the combination of its two separate consumer and commercial Copilot apps last month. That’s a long-overdue change, alongside some big AI leadership shapeups that helped finally appoint a single Copilot boss for the first time.

It’s fair to say that Copilot has failed in the consumer space compared to Claude or ChatGPT, but Microsoft’s core commercial customers are slowly showing interest. This new Copilot app isn’t really designed to compete with things like Muse, and Microsoft is now calling it “the AI built for work.” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also calls Copilot a new operating system. “We’re building Copilot as a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task,” says Nadella in a post on X.

Microsoft is even comparing its new Copilot to how influential Office was on productivity. “Just as Office defined work for the PC era, the new Copilot is built to define it for the AI era,” says Spataro.

That might well be Microsoft’s goal, but there’s a lot more competition in this AI era than there ever was in the PC era. Microsoft has certainly fallen behind the likes of Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and now Meta, and it’ll be interesting to see if “the AI built for work” is enough to help it catch up.

Update, September 25th: Article updated with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella’s comments.

该主题下的文章将被添加到您的每日邮件文摘和主页推送中。
全新 Copilot 融合了 AI 聊天、代码编写和 Autopilot 智能体代理。
该作者的文章将被添加到您的每日邮件文摘和主页推送中。
查看汤姆·沃伦（Tom Warren）的全部文章
继上个月对全新 Copilot“超级应用”进行预热后，微软于今天正式将其公之于众。这款经过重新设计的 Copilot 应用将聊天、编程和智能体三项 AI 能力整合到了单一界面中。作为此次发布的一部分，微软还将今年早些时候在 Build 大会上亮相的 AI 个人助手 Scout 更名为 Autopilot。
这款全新的 Copilot 应用将包含“主页”（Home）、“代码”（Code）和“Autopilot”三个标签页，其中“主页”将 Copilot Chat 与 Cowork 结合在一起。这是 Copilot 用户的默认落地体验，微软还计划在其中加入一项名为“今日”（Today）的功能，充当重要邮件、会议邀请、Teams 讨论帖等的个性化仪表盘。
“主页是让你理清方向、脚踏实地并稳步推进工作的地方：回顾最近的活动、获取 Copilot 能提供哪些帮助的建议，以及无缝衔接之前中断的工作，”微软工作场景 AI 首席营销官贾里德·斯帕塔罗（Jared Spataro）解释道。
“代码”标签页是这款所谓“超级应用”中出人意料的新增功能，通常人们不会将此类功能与面向知识工作者的应用联系在一起。它将允许任何人创建应用程序、跟踪器、仪表盘或自动化流程，并将成果作为云端托管的内部应用分享给同事。“依托与 GitHub Copilot 相同的底层技术，Code 在沙盒环境中运行，并可以在你的租户内实现安全托管，”斯帕塔罗表示。
Autopilot 是 Copilot 体验的新增功能，斯帕塔罗将其形容为一个“数字化队友”。它此前名为 Scout，最初是一款桌面应用，而 Autopilot 则是其云端对应版本，可让个人 AI 助手在你入睡时继续运行。与许多其他 AI 智能体一样，Autopilot 拥有自己的云端计算机实例，可以被指派执行监控 Teams 频道、运行周期性工作任务或处理跟进事项等任务。
与其他一些 AI 智能体相比，真正的区别在于微软将 Autopilot 打造为企业级产品，吸引那些依赖其 Office 和身份管理套件的企业。“Autopilot 驻留在你的租户中，拥有自己的身份、记忆、计算机和工作空间，并且它基于 Microsoft IQ 构建，因此它理解你的组织是如何实际运作的，”斯帕塔罗说。“它出现在人们日常工作的场景中——Teams、Outlook、聊天、频道和文档中——因此你可以像对待同事一样@它，并且背后有完善的权限、审计和治理机制保障。”
所有这些对企业安全和控制的重视，是微软试图再次向企业推销 Copilot 的重要手段。这次的不同之处在于，企业为 Copilot 支付的费用将取决于其员工在做什么。微软对这款新 Copilot 应用中的 Cowork、Code 和 Autopilot 部分采用按用量计费模式，因此任何长时间运行的智能体功能，或对 Astra 和 Fable 等模型的使用，都将按用量收费。
常规的 Copilot 许可证（即用户订阅许可证）将允许你在 Chat 以及 Word、Excel、PowerPoint、Outlook 和 Teams 中使用 Copilot。微软采用自动模型选择器来为每项任务匹配合适的模型，但 IT 管理员需要使用微软全新的“AI 财务运营”（FinOps for AI）工具来管理 AI 开支，确保任何智能体的使用不会失控。
有了这款新的 Copilot 应用，微软似乎终于为其 AI 助手敲定了一套行之有效的方案。自从 Copilot 作为必应（Bing）内部的聊天机器人推出以来，该公司已多次对其进行重新设计，而最新的三标签页设计正是在上个月将原本独立的消费级和商业级 Copilot 应用合二为一的基础上演化而来。这是一场迟到已久的变革，与此同时进行的一系列重大的 AI 领导层重组，也终于促成了首次任命一位统一的 Copilot 负责人。
平心而论，与 Claude 或 ChatGPT 相比，Copilot 在消费端领域算是遭遇了挫折，但微软的核心商业客户正在逐渐展现出兴趣。这款新的 Copilot 应用实际上并非为了与 Muse 之类产品竞争而设计，微软现在将其称为“为工作打造的 AI”。微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉（Satya Nadella）还将 Copilot 称为全新的操作系统。“我们正在将 Copilot 打造为面向工作的全新操作系统，它跨越每一种模型、每一种形态以及每一项任务，”纳德拉在 X 平台发帖表示。
微软甚至将新款 Copilot 的影响力与 Office 对生产力变革的影响力相提并论。“正如 Office 定义了 PC 时代的工作方式一样，全新 Copilot 旨在定义 AI 时代的工作方式，”斯帕塔罗说道。
这很可能是微软的目标，但在这个 AI 时代，竞争远比 PC 时代要激烈得多。微软在这一领域显然已经落后于谷歌（Google）、OpenAI、Anthropic 以及如今的 Meta 等对手，而这款“为工作打造的 AI”是否足以帮助其迎头赶上，仍有待观察。

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: Here's what happens to the economy when Treasury yields soar like they are now
sourceOnlyStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: Government debt costs leaped higher Wednesday, the product of multiple factors.
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
Soaring Treasury yields aren't just bad for the government and its $40 trillion debt. They also threaten to raise borrowing costs, hitting everyone from homeowners to credit card users, while providing limited help to savers and potential benefits to banks.

Government debt costs leaped higher this week, the product of multiple factors including a fresh report revealing heightened inflation pressures, surging expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in October and an auction for 5-year notes showing that Treasury demand was weak. Competition from hyperscaler debt issuance also is seen as an aggravating factor.

Yields responded by jumping more than they have in nearly a year and a half, dating back to April 2025 when President Donald Trump first announced so-called reciprocal tariffs against U.S. trading partners. Recent market liquidity efforts pushed by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have had no impact so far, with rates surging higher despite intensified buyback efforts on longer-dated debt.

The 10-year note, a benchmark for mortgages and other longer-term borrowing, saw its yield hit 5.19%, a level not seen since before the global financial crisis. Similarly, the 2-year note, which typically responds to Fed rate expectations and signals rates for home equity, auto loans and other debt, climbed more than 13 basis points past 4.9% as traders priced in a strong possibility that the central bank would follow its hike last week with another in October.

One basis point equals 0.01% and yields move opposite prices.

Such moves generally portend higher borrowing rates that hit the U.S. economy where it hurts the most — consumers, who drive almost 70% of all economic activity and hold nearly $19 trillion in total debt.

While savers will benefit with incrementally higher rates on their bank savings accounts, it's unlikely to offset the pain they'll feel elsewhere, said Dan North, senior economist with Allianz Trade North America.

"The consumer's the most important part of the economy," North said. "They're going from little tiny yields on savings to ever slightly bigger tiny yields on savings. So I don't think that really yet helps the consumer that much. But it sure does crush housing, and it [impacts] on all those personal consumer loans, the credit cards and so forth."

Indeed, the interest rate on plain-vanilla savings accounts is around 0.37% and has been on a modest decline since the Fed enacted three quarter-point cuts late in 2025, according to Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. data.

Mortgage rates, though, have been on an entirely different trajectory and are likely to continue rising. A typical 30-year mortgage is now at 7.26%, up more than a quarter percentage point in just the past couple of weeks and nearly a full point over the past year, according to Mortgage News Daily.

Credit card interest rates have been fairly steady over the past few years, but also are unlikely to stay that way if current trends hold up.

When the Fed hikes, it feeds directly into the prime rate, which is used as a baseline for adjustable-rate credit and most recently was at 7%, after rising a quarter point off last week's Fed move.

Taken together, the factors make it more expensive for consumers to borrow and less likely that they'll seek the loans and credit that fuel a lot of the activity in the $32 trillion U.S. economy.

"You raise the fed funds rate, rates in the short term and effectively all along the curve go up," North said. "If it makes it harder for somebody to buy a car, then there's less demand for cars and there's less demand for auto workers, and the economy slows down. That's sort of basic economics, but that's how it works."

There are some positives from the higher rates.

Aside from whatever gains savers get, banks can benefit. The industry's model is based on a variety of factors that can benefit in times of higher rates. This includes what banks charge their borrowers and the margin these institutions earn, as well as the interest they pay to depositors.

However, even bank stocks were mostly lower Wednesday as dramatically higher yields could slow loan demand and broader economic activity, which otherwise has been solid. The Atlanta Fed is tracking GDP growth of 5.1% for the third quarter, another element that could be factoring into higher yields.

Persistently higher yields, though, pose dangers to that growth picture.

"Smaller and medium enterprises are going to be suffering the worst because they have less ability to borrow," North said. "Less availability of credit makes it more difficult."

sourceOnlyStories.source: The Guardian Society (卫报社会与民生)
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: Syngenta denies keeping relevant data from the EPA as paraquat stays in the US market despite global bans Sweden started ringing the alarm bell more than 20 years ago, calling for a ban on the weedkilling chemical paraquat in 2004. sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
Syngenta denies keeping relevant data from the EPA as paraquat stays in the US market despite global bans

Sweden started ringing the alarm bell more than 20 years ago, calling for a ban on the weedkilling chemical paraquat in 2004. One by one, dozens of other countries did the same as evidence of paraquat risks to human health mounted. Even the Chinese government, which owns the longtime paraquat maker Syngenta , halted domestic use of the pesticide a decade ago after conducting its own studies on paraquat safety and finding troubling results.

In the US, two states – Vermont and California – have recently also banned paraquat, citing risks that include an association between paraquat and Parkinson’s disease shown in years of scientific research. And California regulators announced in August that paraquat makers voluntarily agreed to stop selling the chemical after the state identified health concerns in connection with its use in new research. Several federal lawmakers have pushed for a nationwide ban.

sourceOnlyStories.originalTitle: APEC leaders to adopt joint declaration at summit in China — Russian Foreign Ministry
sourceOnlyStories.snippet: The Russian delegation is actively preparing for the upcoming APEC summit, Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko pointed out
sourceOnlyStories.fullContent:
MOSCOW, September 25. /TASS/. The APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, scheduled for November 18-19, will allow for the adoption of a substantial package of documents setting the region’s future course, including a joint declaration to be signed by the association’s leaders, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko said in an interview with TASS.

"At the Shenzhen summit, a substantial package of documents is expected to be agreed, which, in addition to the leaders’ declaration, will include policy statements outlining the region’s future course on further developing connectivity, the digital economy and artificial intelligence. Intensive negotiations on these documents are already underway," the diplomat noted. "We are seeking to ensure that the agreements reflect our national approaches and best practices in these areas."

The Russian delegation is actively preparing for the upcoming APEC summit, Rudenko pointed out. "Like our Chinese partners, we are interested in the success of this key regional format this year."

According to the Russian deputy foreign minister, the forum’s work under China’s chairmanship is proceeding intensively and constructively. "The agenda includes issues important for the Asia-Pacific region, such as maintaining growth momentum, preserving open markets and promoting innovation," the diplomat said. "The stage of sectoral ministerial conferences is practically complete, with 11 high-level events held across the entire range of practical cooperation areas."

In addition, Rudenko said, decisions have been adopted to ensure "the effective functioning of energy and food markets, cooperation in forestry, bridging the digital divide and combating the spread of protectionism."

成果文件的利益分配：俄方主张确保协议体现其国家方案与最佳实践，而其他成员经济体对人工智能、数字经济治理规范的主导权可能存在竞合。
blindSpots: 信息源高度单一，仅依赖俄副外长单一官方信源表态，缺乏东道主中国及其他APEC关键经济体（如美、日、东盟成员）对宣言能否顺利达成的多方核实。
回避了地缘政治对抗对多边机制的实际冲击，未提及西方经济体是否会阻挠达成共识性联合宣言。

worldStories.fullContent: (ANSA) - ROMA, 25 SET - The Italian Ambassador to Bulgaria, Marcello Apicella, took part in the press conference for the 22nd edition of the Cinelibri International Film and Literature Festival, conceived by publisher Jacqueline Wagenstein, which was held on September 24 at the Military Club in the capital. Also present at the press conference was Irina Dakova, Deputy Mayor of Sofia responsible for culture and tourism. In his remarks, Ambassador Apicella noted how Italian cinema has introduced Italy to the world and enhanced our country’s image globally. He then highlighted Italian cinema’s extraordinary ability to tell modest stories imbued with universal values—that is, its capacity to unite the particular with the universal. The third edition of Italian Screens, one of the leading international initiatives dedicated to promoting Italian cinema abroad and supported by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, the Ministry of Culture, and Cinecittà, will feature screenings of eight Italian films released between 2024 and 2026 and is distinguished by its rich variety of themes. Among the selected titles: “Brunello, the Gentle Visionary,” which explores the life and philosophy of Umbrian entrepreneur Brunello Cucinelli; “The Girl with the Leica,” a passionate portrait of Gerda Taro, a young photographer and reporter who died during the Spanish Civil War; “Francesca and Giovanni – A Story of Love and the Mafia,” which recounts the lives of Italian magistrates Francesca Morvillo and Giovanni Falcone, highlighting how behind the great chapters of Italian history lie people, emotions, choices, and courage; “A Story,” a reflection on identity and the difficulty of change; “The Chilean,” a tale of the intertwining and overlapping vicissitudes of Chilean and Italian national histories; “L’amore che ho,” a tribute to Rosa Balistreri, an icon of 20th-century Sicilian folk music; “Scherzetto,” a reflection on the passage of time and the difficult relationship between who we once were and who we have become. The Italian Gala Evening of the third edition of Italian Screens, which will take place on October 17 at the Cinema Lumière, will open with a screening of Nanni Moretti’s film “Succederà questa notte,” based on a collection of short stories by Israeli writer Eshkol Nevo. The film, which premiered in Venice, is an ensemble comedy about human relationships, love, and the possibility of changing something when we least expect it. Festival Director Jacqueline Wagenstein emphasized that audience members will have the opportunity to meet some of the directors and lead actors featured in the films on the program. The festival will take place from October 15 to November 8 in Sofia and seven other cities across Bulgaria: Plovdiv, Varna, Burgas, Veliko Tarnovo, Gabrovo, Stara Zagora, and Pernik. The program will be organized with the support of the Sofia Municipality, the National Film Center, and the respective municipalities.
worldStories.fullTranslation:
（安莎社）- 罗马，9月25日 - 意大利驻保加利亚大使马塞洛·阿皮切拉（Marcello Apicella）出席了第22届“电影与文学”（Cinelibri）国际电影节的新闻发布会。该电影节由出版人雅克琳·瓦根施泰因（Jacqueline Wagenstein）发起，发布会于9月24日在保加利亚首都的军事俱乐部举行。负责文化和旅游事务的索非亚副市长伊琳娜·达科娃（Irina Dakova）也出席了新闻发布会。阿皮切拉大使在致辞中指出，意大利电影如何向世界展示了意大利，并提升了国家在全球的形象。他随后强调了意大利电影在讲述蕴含普世价值观的质朴故事方面的卓越能力——即其将特殊性与普遍性相融合的能力。

作为致力于在海外推广意大利电影的重要国际举措之一，“意大利银幕”（Italian Screens）由意大利外交与国际合作部、文化部和奇尼奇塔（Cinecittà）共同支持。本次举办的第三届活动将展映8部于2024年至2026年间发行的意大利电影，题材丰富多样。入选影片包括：探索翁布里亚企业家布鲁内洛·库奇内利（Brunello Cucinelli）生活与哲学的《布鲁内洛：温和的远见者》（Brunello, the Gentle Visionary）；生动刻画在西班牙内战中牺牲的年轻摄影师兼记者格尔达·塔罗（Gerda Taro）的《拿徕卡的女孩》（The Girl with the Leica）；讲述意大利法官弗朗西斯卡·莫尔维洛（Francesca Morvillo）与乔瓦尼·法尔科内（Giovanni Falcone）生平的《弗朗西斯卡与乔瓦尼——关于爱与黑手党的故事》（Francesca and Giovanni – A Story of Love and the Mafia），影片强调在意大利历史的重大篇章背后，存在着真实的人、情感、选择与勇气；反思身份认同与改变之艰难的《一个故事》（A Story）；讲述智利与意大利两国国家历史交织交叠沧桑变迁的《智利人》（The Chilean）；致敬20世纪西西里民谣标志性人物罗莎·巴利斯特里（Rosa Balistreri）的《我的爱》（L’amore che ho）；以及反思岁月流逝和“曾经的我们”与“现在的我们”之间复杂关系的《小恶作剧》（Scherzetto）。

第三届“意大利银幕”的意大利盛大之夜活动将于10月17日在卢米埃尔影院（Cinema Lumière）举行，届时将以放映南尼·莫莱蒂（Nanni Moretti）执导的影片《今夜将发生》（Succederà questa notte）拉开帷幕。该片改编自以色列作家埃什科尔·内沃（Eshkol Nevo）的短篇小说集，曾在威尼斯电影节首映，是一部关于人际关系、爱情以及在我们最意想不到时改变现状的可能性的群像喜剧。

电影节总监雅克琳·瓦根施泰因强调，观众将有机会与展映影片的部分导演和主演面对面交流。该电影节将于10月15日至11月8日在索非亚及保加利亚其他七座城市举行，包括普罗夫迪夫、瓦尔纳、布尔加斯、大特尔诺沃、加布罗沃、旧扎戈拉和佩尔尼克。该展映项目将在索非亚市政府、保加利亚国家电影中心以及各相关城市市政府的支持下组织开展。

November WTI crude oil futures spent the week trading a possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz against the risk that shipping conditions have not normalized. The contract fell to $88.67 Tuesday after reports that Iran could reopen the Strait within seven days, then recovered to $96.78 Thursday as the diplomatic story ran into the same problem it had all week: no agreement, no normal tanker traffic, and no proof the physical market is back to normal.

At 22:00 GMT Thursday, November, WTI crude oil futures were trading at $94.76, down $0.71 or 0.74% for the week. The market is off the week’s high, but it is also well above Tuesday’s low. That tells the story. Traders took premium out when Saudi barrels started moving, and Iran floated a deal. They put some of it back when it became clear that workaround routes are not the same as open shipping lanes.

Saudi and Iraqi Barrels Changed the Crude Trade

The week started with more crude getting through a market that had been priced for a bigger supply problem. Saudi Aramco increased shipments through Hormuz after attacks damaged its East-West Pipeline and interrupted some Red Sea loadings. Tanker tracking showed about 14 million barrels loaded on seven VLCCs inside the Gulf. Saudi flows through the Strait rose sharply from August levels.

The East-West Pipeline restart added another option. It was not a full return to normal capacity, but it gave Saudi Arabia a route to the Red Sea that did not require every…

The East-West Pipeline restart added another option. It was not a full return to normal capacity, but it gave Saudi Arabia a route to the Red Sea that did not require every barrel to pass through Hormuz. Iraq also said it could raise exports through Turkey.

Those are actual barrels and actual routes. That is why crude sold off before the market had a diplomatic agreement. Traders do not need a peace deal to cut some premium if more oil can reach buyers.

The trade is still expensive and fragile. Producers are using ship-to-ship transfers off Oman, military escorts and changed loading plans to keep exports moving. The barrels are moving, but they are moving through a system that costs more, takes longer, and can break again on one attack. Reuters reported that visible vessel traffic through Hormuz remains far below pre-war levels, even as producers keep exports moving through workarounds.

Iran Offered a Path, Not an Opening

Tuesday’s sell-off accelerated after Kyodo News reported that Iran could reopen Hormuz within seven days if the United States eased military pressure. The market sold the headline as if the Strait were already reopening.

It was never that simple. Iran’s position was conditional. The United States did not announce a deal. Insurance, safe passage, tanker traffic and refined-product flows did not suddenly return to normal.

The reason is straightforward. The two sides had a similar framework earlier in the year, and it broke down. A report about talks changes expectations. It does not change the route until tankers are moving without military escort and the insurance market starts pricing less risk.

Diesel Is Not Following Crude Lower

The crude market found supply relief this week. The diesel market did not.

European gasoil’s premium to Brent reached a record near $95 per barrel. U.S. diesel prices remain above $6 per gallon. The product shortage comes from disrupted refinery and product flows, not a lack of crude alone.

That distinction matters. Saudi Arabia can redirect a crude cargo. Iraq can move more oil through Turkey. Neither action creates a barrel of diesel for Europe when Middle East product flows are impaired, and refiners are already running hard.

The White House added another layer when Politico reported that the administration was considering a 90-day diesel export ban. The White House later denied the report. The policy is not in place, but the idea showed where the pressure is building. Restricting exports may add barrels inside the United States. It also removes supply from Europe, which is already paying record premiums for distillate.

The product market is still telling crude traders not to become too comfortable with the supply relief. Crude can fall on a report about Saudi exports. Diesel needs refinery output and normal trade flows before its premium comes out.

Inventory Data Showed the Same Split

The EIA reported that U.S. commercial crude inventories rose 3 million barrels to 426.4 million barrels in the week ended September 18. Analysts had expected a draw. That gave sellers another reason to press crude after Saudi and Iraqi supply options improved.

Distillate inventories told a different story. Stocks fell 428,000 barrels to 107.4 million barrels. The draw was not large, but it came with diesel and gasoil premiums already at extreme levels.

Commercial crude is adding. Refined-product supply remains tight. The Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen toward 285 million barrels, leaving less cushion behind the commercial system. That is why the crude and diesel markets can send different signals during the same week.

Weekly November WTI Crude Oil Futures Technical Analysis

Trend Indicator Analysis

November WTI crude oil futures are edging higher for the week, but the market is close to posting a weekly closing price reversal top. The contract reached a new main top at $101.69 before turning lower. Last week’s close was $95.86. A weekly close below that level would confirm the reversal pattern. It would not change the main trend, which remains up, but it could shift momentum to the downside.

The nearest minor bottom is $78.55, and the main bottom is $67.09. The short-term retracement target is the 50% level at $90.12. The main 50% level at $84.39 is the next downside target. Both sit well above the rising 52-week moving average at $70.62. On the upside, a trade through $101.69 resumes the uptrend and opens the door to former tops at $104.44 and $110.08.

Weekly Technical Forecast

The direction of the Weekly November Crude Oil futures contract for the week ending October 2 is likely to be determined by trader reaction to $95.18.

A sustained move above $95.18 will signal the presence of buyers. This will put the market in a position to possibly retest the contract high at $101.69 if the headlines turn bullish again. Potential upside targets include $104.44 and $110.08.

A sustained move under $95.18 will indicate that buying is slowing and that selling pressure is increasing. If it creates enough downside momentum, then we could see a retest of $88.67. A trade through this level will send a strong signal that the rally is weakening, with $84.39 and $78.67 as other potential targets.

The market has reduced the odds of an immediate Gulf supply shock, but it has not priced in a normal oil trade. Saudi barrels are moving. Iraq is adding supply options. Ship-to-ship transfers are keeping some Gulf crude flowing. Those developments limit the upside as long as they continue.

The risk is that traders have already discounted the diplomatic story twice without receiving a deal. If talks produce tanker flows, lower insurance costs, and normal shipping through Hormuz, more premium can come out of crude. If the talks fail, another attack hits Saudi infrastructure, or diesel inventories keep falling, the physical market will take control again.

The week’s range from $97.22 to $88.67, then back to $96.78 shows how quickly the market can reprice in both directions. The crude market has supply relief. The diesel market still has a shortage.

Technically, a closing price reversal top was produced at $101.69 the week ending September 18. This means we’re not looking at an ordinary top. Besides being a bearish indicator, it’s also a trigger point for an acceleration to the upside. So keep that in mind if it is taken out by renewed buying.

The downside targets are 50% levels. They include $90.12, $84.39, and $78.67. Buyers will treat them as value levels. Since the main trend is up, the market is still likely in “buy the dip” mode.

It isn’t until sellers start taking out swing bottoms at $78.55, $72.05, and $67.09 that traders are going to have to worry about a change in trend.

Most of all, the 52-week moving average at $71.21 is still holding the major long-term trend intact.
